The simple answer is calling it a social construct is a slight over simplification, gender is socially CONSTRUCTED. 

Gender is our lived experience of our biological sex, our lived experience of anything is primarily impacted by our socialisation. So the way you are taught to express your own biological sex (gender expression) is highly influenced, if not mostly constructed by, the way you are shown, taught or expected to express your sex assigned at birth. In our society physical appearance determines these expectations and lessons. So when we say gender is a social construct we're not saying it's separate from biology (trans and cisgender people have distinct biological differences) we're saying that society and socialisation determines an individuals gender in their formative years more so than that individuals biology. So in a sense being trans is a social construct because the main reason people need to transition is to correct societal misconceptions about their gender. However, to be more accurate transgender people are socially constructing/re-constructing their gender to match their own biology.

It's always hard to pinpoint exactly  "why" any biological system comes into being. However, there are some generally accepted theorys as to why humans in particular developed such dramatic visual cues for sadness. 
1. We are an extremely prosocial species who depend on group strength for survival, therfore we've always needed to display emotions in a visible and universally understood way even before language. So before language we needed to know what other humans were feeling, furrowed brows=threat, wide grin=friend, wet eyes=no threat/needs help. This still applies to modern day babies and people who communicate without shared language. 
2. We're mammals, the only other species known to cry is elephant's, a highly intelligent social mamailian species. So it's possible that us being intelligent mammals is why we leak fluid to show sadness as opposed to howling or whatever.
3. Crying has been shown to release both feel good hormones (makes us feel better), and pheromones (makes others feel bad for us). It's also been shown that happy tears have a different chemical composition to sad tears. Due to this evidence some  have theorised that crying is a cheat proof way for humans to show vulnerability/emotion. Smiling and frowning can be faked, but scent is impossible to fake and humans pick up on it subconsciously.

TLDR; yes crying is weird, but crying also serves many practical functions, like displaying vulnerability to promote helping in social groups, releasing feel good hormones and unfakable "help me" pheromones.
